name: @atlas/db
description: Prisma schema, migrations, and the shared PrismaClient singleton

comments.dotenv: Prisma looks for .env next to the schema or in the cwd, and finds neither in a workspace. dotenv-cli points every command at the single repository-root .env so there is exactly one place a connection string is configured. These scripts require that file to exist — `cp .env.example .env` first.
comments.postinstall: The generated client is a build artifact, not source, so it is gitignored — which means a fresh clone has no Prisma types until something generates them. Without this hook `npm install && npm run dev` fails on the first request with implicit-any errors, since $transaction's callback parameter has nothing to infer from. Generation needs no DATABASE_URL and no .env, so it is safe to run unconditionally at install time. CI and both Dockerfiles still call db:generate explicitly; generation is idempotent, so the duplication costs a few hundred milliseconds and keeps those pipelines readable on their own.
